reasoning: Both attempts keep server code on the server, mark the client module ClientOnly, ship the remote as a child of the network module, and send the too-far message through NotificationServerService. B mirrors the SystemPackage/Implementation split properly, with generic services and game-specific setup and mediator modules, and uses absolute requires that work on both realms. A leaves Implementation empty, puts game wiring in the SystemPackage, and its relocated client module reaches Catalogs and Utilities through risky relative requires. A's validation and specs are slightly stronger, but B's structure and require correctness count for more.

criteria.note: PlacementSystem is under Systems/Building with SystemPackage and a network module holding the remote, but Implementation/ has only init.meta.json. Game wiring (baseplate lookup, MAX_REACH) lives in PlacementServerService.

criteria.note: PlacementServerService.meta.json and PlacementRules.meta.json both set RelocateToServerScriptService: true.

No blocking waits in top level, Init or Start
criteria.note: PlaceBlock ships as a model.json child of PlacementNetwork, so the WaitForChild on script resolves at once; Init and Start only connect events.

Checks the type via BlockTypes.ByName, Vector3 and finite values via isSanePosition with bounds, the floor via isAboveFloor, occupancy via occupiedCells, 64-stud reach and 10/s. Notifies only when too far, keys 1-5 only, click plus tap detection.
Typed, clean code with a spec; selene and StyLua pass, and the luau-lsp failure is a tool path error. The rate limit counts invalid requests too, which is stricter than asked.

Checks the type, Vector3 plus NaN-safe snap tolerance, floor, occupancy (blocksByCell), MaxDistance 64 and 10/s on successful placements. NUMBER_KEYS runs to Nine, so it goes past 1-5 if the catalog grows.
Typed code with RejectReason union types; selene and StyLua pass, and the luau-lsp failure is a tool path error. It relies on SetRules running before the first request (assert).

strengths: Thorough validation, including world bounds and NaN or infinite values
Pure PlacementRules module with Jest specs
Too-far notifications throttled, sent through NotificationServerService
Exact 1-5 keys and its own tap detection
weaknesses: Implementation folder is empty; game-specific wiring sits in SystemPackage
Relative requires from the relocated client module to Catalogs and Utilities may fail on clients

strengths: Clean generic SystemPackage plus game-specific Implementation split
Rejection-callback mediator keeps the notification dependency out of the service
Absolute requires that work on both realms
Tag-based targeting and TouchTapInWorld for taps
